name: aadb-eval-seed
description: Synthetic current-app topology generation cases captured through the AADB v2 prompt and post-processing contract.

cases.title: Concise three-tier web application
cases.prompt: Design a secure, production-ready three-tier web application on Azure with a browser frontend, an API, a relational database, and image storage. Include identity and operational monitoring.
cases.expectedBehavior: Produce a connected three-tier topology with an internet-facing entry point, application compute, relational data, object storage, Microsoft Entra ID, secrets protection, and a sparse monitoring path. The architecture may use any suitable managed Azure web and database services.

cases.title: Event-driven order processing
cases.prompt: Design an event-driven order platform that handles 50,000 orders per hour. External clients enter through API Management. Use asynchronous orchestration, idempotent workers, durable order state, inventory updates, session caching, dead-letter handling, Microsoft Entra ID, Key Vault, and end-to-end monitoring. Prefer managed services and isolate synchronous request handling from background fulfillment.
cases.expectedBehavior: Separate synchronous order acceptance from asynchronous processing. Show API ingress, a durable messaging broker, managed compute workers, transactional order state, cache, identity, secrets, and observability. Messaging connections must be marked asynchronous and the workflow must cover acceptance, enqueueing, processing, persistence, and failure handling.

cases.title: Private PaaS and zero trust
cases.prompt: Design a zero-trust customer portal using Azure Front Door Premium with WAF, API Management, Container Apps, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and Blob Storage. PaaS data services must use Private Link, application secrets must use Key Vault, outbound traffic must be controlled, administrators must not expose SSH or public database endpoints, and authentication must use Microsoft Entra ID. Include Defender for Cloud and centralized monitoring.
cases.expectedBehavior: Create a layered edge, application, private data, security, and operations topology. PaaS data services should be represented behind Private Link or private endpoints, identity should protect the application rather than act as the user's first destination, and no public administrative path should be introduced.

cases.title: Enterprise RAG agent
cases.prompt: Create an internal AI assistant for employees that answers questions from approved company documents with citations, respects each user's permissions, supports feedback, and can be operated safely by a small platform team. Use Microsoft Foundry and managed Azure services. Make reasonable assumptions explicit in the workflow.
cases.expectedBehavior: Produce a defensible retrieval-augmented generation design with authenticated application ingress, Microsoft Foundry or Azure OpenAI, indexed approved content, durable source storage, identity-aware retrieval, secrets, feedback or conversation state, content safeguards, and monitoring. The workflow should distinguish ingestion/indexing from the online query path and mention assumptions through its descriptions.

cases.title: Intelligent document processing bridge
cases.prompt: Design a managed intelligent document processing platform. Users upload PDFs and images through a protected API. Store originals, extract text and fields with Azure AI Document Intelligence, classify and summarize content with Azure OpenAI, index searchable content in Azure AI Search, persist document status and metadata, quarantine failed or suspicious files, and include Microsoft Entra ID, Key Vault, asynchronous orchestration, and monitoring.
cases.expectedBehavior: Show a chronological upload, durable storage, asynchronous processing, extraction, AI enrichment, indexing, metadata persistence, quarantine, and operations flow. Required services must be connected through their primary data path and background processing must be distinguished from synchronous upload handling.

cases.title: Real-time IoT analytics
cases.prompt: Design an industrial IoT monitoring platform for 5,000 devices sending telemetry every five seconds. Require secure device provisioning, a hot path for sub-second anomaly dashboards, a cool path retaining raw data for seven years, predictive maintenance scoring, operator alerts, replay after downstream outages, private connectivity where supported, and centralized health monitoring. Use managed Azure services.
cases.expectedBehavior: Separate hot and cool telemetry paths from secure device ingestion through streaming processing, operational visualization, durable raw storage, predictive scoring, and alerting. The topology should include a dedicated dashboard service and asynchronous event flow.

cases.title: Microsoft Fabric medallion analytics
cases.prompt: Design a Microsoft Fabric medallion lakehouse that ingests batch and streaming sources into OneLake, processes Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers, serves a Direct Lake semantic model and Power BI reporting, includes data governance and operational monitoring, and runs on an explicit Fabric capacity.
cases.expectedBehavior: Represent Fabric ingestion, OneLake, medallion processing, curated serving, semantic modeling, reporting, governance, and the billed Fabric capacity. Fabric items must be grouped under Microsoft Fabric and the workflow must distinguish batch and streaming paths when both are present.

cases.title: Multi-region regulated commerce bridge
cases.prompt: Design a PCI-regulated commerce platform active in two Azure regions with a 15-minute RPO and one-hour RTO. It must survive a regional failure, keep checkout latency low, process orders asynchronously, maintain a globally available product catalog, protect payment traffic, centralize secrets and audit telemetry, and minimize standing infrastructure cost. The business asks for strict regional data residency while also requesting globally writable customer and order data; resolve that tension safely in the architecture and workflow.
cases.expectedBehavior: Produce a multi-region design with global protected ingress, regional application stacks, asynchronous order processing, caching, resilient data services, secrets, and observability. The workflow should explicitly resolve the conflict between global writes and strict residency, for example by keeping regulated records region-bound while globally distributing nonregulated catalog data.
